subject: Post-call recap & MAP draft: Integration build plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acmemaps.com>, Carlos Reyes <c.reyes@acmemaps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & MAP draft: Integration build plan

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Acme Maps' roadmap for live routing and embedded navigation. As promised, attached is a first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the integration milestone we discussed: SDK integration, streaming responses, tool calling for geofence lookups, and structured outputs for your internal analytics pipeline.

Quick recap / asks:
- Target close date (commercial + legal sign-off): proposed 2027-05-01. Please confirm if that works on your side.
- Key milestone we want to align on now: Integration build plan (milestones, owners, dependencies).
- Next step: If you’re comfortable, please review the attached MAP and let us know owners for the technical milestones (we've stubbed owners but want your confirmation). I’ve cc'd Marissa (engineering lead) and David (sales ops/procurement) to help fill technical/contract items.

High-level MAP milestone (draft):
1) SDK integration PoC (owner: Marissa) — 2 weeks
2) Streaming & low-latency validation (owner: Marissa) — 3 weeks
3) Tool calling integration (geofence lookups) (owner: Acme eng / Marissa) — 2 weeks
4) Structured output schema and analytics pipeline (owner: Carlos/Acme) — 1 week
5) End-to-end QA + perf validation (owner: Marissa) — 1 week

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.xlsx, redwood_map_sdk_integration_spec.pdf

Would it help if Marissa shared a more detailed milestone table with owners and dates?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap and draft MAP. A few quick items from our side:
- Target close date: 2027-05-01 is our goal but procurement will need at least 3 weeks to process (so sooner confirmations on pricing/terms help).
- Technical question: for streaming + low-latency, can Redwood support server-sent events/keep-alive streaming from the SDK, or do we need a proxied streaming service? We want to avoid adding extra infra if possible.
- For tool calling: we plan to host the geofence service in our VPC, would Redwood's tool-calling model call an HTTP endpoint in our VPC, or must it be exposed publicly?

I’ll loop in our eng lead (Carlos) to coordinate owners. Procurement is cc'd to start preparing PO process.

— Sofia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acmemaps.com>, Carlos Reyes <c.reyes@acmemaps.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & MAP draft: Integration build plan — technical owners & dates

Hi team — attached is a more detailed Integration Build Plan (see attached spec + MAP update). Answers inline below and owners assigned.

Short answers to Sofia's questions:
- Streaming: Redwood SDK supports streaming via HTTP/2 chunked responses and server-sent event style responses in our managed SDKs. For private deployments we can also configure a proxied long-lived websocket if you prefer. No extra customer infra required by default.
- Tool calling: Redwood's tool-calling can invoke customer endpoints over HTTPS. For VPC-hosted services we support VPC peering/private-link options (requires network setup on Acme side). If you cannot expose endpoints publicly, we recommend Private deployment or a secure connector.

Integration Build Plan (owner — target dates in UTC — dependencies):
1) SDK integration PoC — Owner: Marissa Cole (Redwood Eng) — 2027-03-22 to 2027-03-29 — Dep: access to Acme staging API keys, sample routes.
2) Streaming validation (end-to-end) — Owner: Marissa Cole — 2027-03-30 to 2027-04-12 — Dep: test dataset, latency SLOs, staging traffic.
3) Tool calling integration (geofence) — Owner: Carlos Reyes (Acme) / Marissa Cole — 2027-04-13 to 2027-04-26 — Dep: network access (VPC peering) or public endpoint, API contract.
4) Structured output schema & analytics pipeline — Owner: Carlos Reyes — 2027-04-27 to 2027-05-03 — Dep: agreed JSON schema for structured outputs.
5) End-to-end QA & perf validation — Owner: Marissa Cole — 2027-05-04 to 2027-05-10 — Dep: signed contract, test harness, perf targets.

Owners and points of contact:
- SDK/Streaming: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.com)
- Tool calling / API contract: Carlos Reyes (c.reyes@acmemaps.com)
- Analytics/schema: Carlos / Acme analytics team
- Procurement/legal: David Kim (david@redwood.com)

Attachments included: redwood_map_sdk_integration_spec.pdf (technical spec), updated MAP workbook (mutual_action_plan_v2.xlsx). I also added a short checklist for network options (public endpoint vs. VPC/private).

I’ll join the next sync to walk through the streaming and tool-calling options.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Engineering Lead, Integrations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_map_sdk_integration_spec.pdf]

Hi Sofia / Procurement team — quick notes on procurement timeline and required artifacts so we can hit the proposed 2027-05-01 close: 
- Standard timeline: 2–3 weeks for PO + legal review after receipt of final SOW and pricing.
- What we will provide immediately: final pricing sheet, standard MSA & SOW, SOC 2 Type II summary, data processing addendum (DPA).
- Action items for Acme: confirm billing contact and whether you need Redwood to sign any marketplace/partner contract.
- Dependencies that could push the target date: negotiated redlines to MSA, enterprise security review (if you require an on-site audit), and network/VPC approvals for private connector setup.

I’ve created a DocuSign envelope for the MSA/SOW placeholders — link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ACME-Redwood-MAP. Once we have the technical milestones locked in and Acme confirms the target dates, I’ll push the final SOW and routing of the DocuSign to procurement.

Regards,
David Kim
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
